generatedCommentsNodes.comment: New test cases are added for scenarios involving `sort` and `where` clauses before `mv_expand` in #BX0QS. These tests should be reviewed to ensure they cover all relevant scenarios, including those where the limit is not explicitly set (default limits) and where the limit is set to zero or a very large number.

The changes in #T0EK8 modify the behavior of `PushDownAndCombineLimits` to handle `MvExpand`. Ensure that this change does not inadvertently affect other parts of the query optimization process, especially when dealing with nested or complex queries involving multiple `MvExpand` operations.

The `assert limit == null;` in #KV2FE suggests that the `limit` should not be serialized on the coordinator node. This might lead to issues if the `limit` is used for any logic that requires coordination between nodes. Ensure that this assumption holds true and document it clearly.
The changes in #2XJF6, #GQMPK, #A6HFN, and #NJRDY modify test cases and serialization tests. Ensure that these changes do not inadvertently break existing functionality or introduce new bugs.

review_comment: Perhaps a comment here might be a good idea. The PR description explains this very nicely, but I imagine someone reading this code later might be a little confused.

Interesting that this code previously did not push the limit down past the MvExpand at all, but the bug reports indicate that that was happening. Was it happening somewhere else? If so, should that location be modified?

Oh yeah, good point, I forgot about it...
We have another rule, called `DuplicateLimitAfterMvExpand`, that does exactly what I describe above: 
`MV_EXPAND | LIMIT` -> `LIMIT | MV_EXPAND | LIMIT`

I think we can remove it

There is another rule, [AddDefaultTopN](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/optimizer/rules/logical/AddDefaultTopN.java), that is intrinsically wrong (it adds an arbitrary limit at the beginning of the query) and that IMHO should be removed as well, but I'm not sure this fix is enough to do it, maybe the problems it tries to solve are not only related to MV_EXPAND.
